3Reading · In context≈ 10 min

Whose camera is this?

Gabriela found a camera and posted online. Read the conversation — notice look like, looks around 35 and What's he like?

Social media post
GabrielaHi everyone. I found a camera on Corona Avenue at about 3 p.m. today. This is the most recent photo on it. Does anyone know these people? Please share this post so we can find out whose camera it is. Thanks!
KatieThe man in the middle looks like Eduardo's brother, but I'm not sure. You can ask Eduardo — he works in the library.
GabrielaI don't know Eduardo. What does he look like?
KatieHe's got dark hair and a beard like the man in the photo, but he doesn't look old. He looks around 35.
GabrielaWhat's he like? Will he think I'm strange if I show him a photo?
KatieNo, don't worry, he won't think you're strange. He's really nice.

Read and choose the right answer:

4Presentation · Grammar≈ 16 min

look like · look + adjective · be like

Five useful patterns for describing people, places and things.

look like + noun
say something is similar to something else
He looks like my mum.
That painting looks like a Magritte.
look + adjective
describe appearance or feeling
You look tired.
Those buildings look old.
look + number
guess someone's age
She looks around 20.
They look over 60.
What … look like?
ask about appearance
A: What does Gregor look like?
B: He looks the same as before.
What … like?
ask about character
A: What are your classmates like?
B: They're really nice.

Good to know: taste, smell, feel and sound work the same way as look: "It smells like fresh bread." · "That sounds fun."

Pronunciation · listen & repeat (5.4)
🎧 What do you notice about the bold letters?
0:00 / 0:00
  • 1Oh dear. You look angry!
  • 2He looks really sad.
  • 3She looks like a runner.
  • 4They look excited.

Notice how look / looks / like link smoothly to the next word. Listen and repeat.

Think about it (talk with your teacher)
  • ◆
    "He looks like my brother." — Is he my brother, or just similar?
  • ◆
    "He looks tired." — Are we talking about how he seems, or his character?
  • ◆
    "What does she look like?" and "What is she like?" — which asks about appearance, which about personality?
  • ◆
    After look like, do we use a noun (my dad) or an adjective (happy)?
  • ◆
    "She looks around 30." — Do we know her exact age?

Task · Guess who (8 min)

Look at the people. Describe one of them — appearance, age and character — but don't say which! Use looks, looks like and is like. Can your teacher guess?
e.g. "This person has dark hair and a beard. He looks creative and quite relaxed…"

Task · Three important people (8 min)

Think of three people who are important to you. Make a few notes, then tell your teacher about them:

  • 1Who is each person?
  • 2Why is each person important to you?
  • 3What does each person look like?
  • 4What is each person like? (character)
  • 5Who are you most similar to or different from — and why?
